paragraphs: On Thursday, the Explorers sat in the school hall beside the stage. Teacher Kim gave them a small job. "The school wants a Jobs Morning," she said. "Please invite three visitors to talk about their careers." Lily opened her notebook, and Mia, Leo, and May sat next to her. The hall was quiet, and the teacher waited.

"Who shall we invite first?" asked Lily. "I want a scientist," said Mia. "A scientist can tell us about animals, and children love animals." "That is a good idea," said May. "A scientist needs a diploma from a university, so the children can learn that school is important." "Yes," said Mia, "and the scientist can show a small experiment on the stage." "Is it safe?" asked Leo. "Yes, and Teacher Kim can stand beside the table," said Mia.

"I want a celebrity," said Leo. "A famous singer can make the morning exciting, and everybody likes music." "But a famous singer is very busy," said Lily, "and he will not come to a school on a weekday." "Then let's ask a musician from our town," said Leo. "He is not a celebrity, but he can play the guitar for us." "That is better," said May, "because the children can meet him again in town." Leo smiled, because he liked the plan.

"Now we need a third visitor," said Lily. "I think a police officer is a good idea," said May. "One police officer stands beside the school gate every morning, and everybody knows her." "What does she do all day?" asked Leo. "She helps children cross the road, and she keeps the street safe," said May. "Shall I write the letter to her?" "Yes, please write it yourself," said Lily, "because you write the best emails."

May took a clean sheet and began to write the letter herself. She wrote, "Dear Police Officer, we invite you to our Jobs Morning." Mia wrote a second letter to the scientist. Leo wrote a third letter to the musician. Lily checked the three letters and drew a small paw print at the bottom of each one. Lily put the letters in a blue folder. Teacher Kim read them and smiled. "Three good visitors and three good reasons," she said. "The Explorers have done a good job today," she added. May carried the blue folder to the school office.
